newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chips end weaker on economic outlook.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chips end weaker on economic outlook.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks ended a shade lower after a roller-coaster session Thursday as an unexpectedly weak August durable goods report left traders scrambling to sell economically sensitive issues.
The broader market fared a bit better, led by selected technology stocks and issues less tied to swings in the economy.

"The durables point to an economic slowdown and fortify the Fed's decision (on Tuesday) not to raise short-term rates," said Peter Cardillo of Westfalia Investments. "But a slowdown raises the question about future corporate earnings."

After early selling and a spate of late morning buying, the Dow Jones industrial average settled down 8.51 points at 5,868.85. In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,388 to 999 on active volume of 499.8 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The technology laden Nasdaq Composite index rose 3.32 points to 1,227.98, but that was well off its 1,237.26 intraday high.

The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond added 17/32 to yield 6.88 percent, down from 6.93 percent at Wednesday's close, as the yield continued falling after the Federal Reserve opted to hold short-term rates steady on Tuesday.

The Commerce Department said orders for big-ticket items fell a surprisingly steep 3.1 percent -- the sharpest drop since April 1995. Separately, the Labour Department said weekly jobless claims jumped by 11,000 to 340,000 for the week ended Sept 21.

A.C. Moore, senior investment strategist at Dunvegan Associates, said that the Dow came under pressure "as the durable goods report showed there won't be the push in earnings for many industrial stocks."
Caterpillar lost 1/2 to 74-1/4, Alcoa was off 1/4 to 59 and International Paper lost 1/4 to 41-7/8.

The Dow Jones Transportation Average slumped 22.83 points, or 1.10 percent, to 2,048.77 as investors shed airline stocks on worries over higher fuel costs and slower domestic travel. UAL, parent of United Airlines, fell 1-1/8 to 45-1/4, American Airlines parent AMR shed 2-1/4 to 79-1/2 and Delta lost 7/8 to 70-1/2.
Defensive stocks like drug, beverage and food issues fared better as they were deemed less vulnerable to economic swings.
Merck rose two to 70-3/4, Coca-Cola added 3/8 to 51-1/2 and Procter & Gamble was up 3/8 to 96-3/8.

Stocks got a late morning boost as word spread that influential Morgan Stanley global strategist Barton Biggs was more bullish on U.S. stocks. Biggs said stocks could rally as much as 10 percent in the short run, citing impressive bond and dollar action after the Fed voted to hold rates steady. "That sent a ripple of enthusiasm to the tape," said Moore.
The final revision to second-quarter Gross Domestic Product is due Friday. A 4.6 percent GDP growth rate is expected after the 4.8 percent reading in the second estimate.
Dow component DuPont rose 1-7/8 to 89 after the company forecast third-quarter earnings would top estimates by at least 10 percent on strength in oil production.
Among initial public offerings, retailer Abercrombie & Fitch, which outfitted the expeditions of Teddy Roosevelt and Ernest Hemingway, surged 7-1/8 to 23-1/8.
Xionics Document Technologies sured 2-3/8 to 14-3/8 in its Wall Street debut. Xionics designs technology for linking office printers, computers and the Internet.
Gap Inc. slumped 1-1/8 to 29-1/2.
Morgan Stanley cut Gap to outperform from strong buy on the belief the retailer's sales gains will be weaker during the rest of the year than in the spring and summer.
Silicon Graphics lost 1-3/8 to 22-1/4 after forecasting first-quarter profits will fall "materially below" market expectations. Morgan Stanley and Dean Witter downgraded the stock.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 0.03 of a point to 685.86. The American Stock Exchange index rose 1.30 to 567.19.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 0.69 to a record 365.99. The average share was up 8 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 6,749.133, up 14.275 or 0.21 percent.
